title: Score Remainder with the Modulo Operator
description:
Compute the **remainder** when each student's score is divided by 10. This is useful for extracting the last digit of a score (e.g. to create grade bins).

**Table: students** — `id`, `name`, `score`

Return `id`, `name`, `score`, and `score % 10` aliased as `remainder`. Order by `id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE students (id INT, name VARCHAR, score INT); INSERT INTO students VALUES (1,'Alice',95),(2,'Bob',82),(3,'Carol',77),(4,'Dave',63),(5,'Eve',91),(6,'Frank',54),(7,'Grace',88);
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, score, score % 10 AS remainder FROM students ORDER BY id

test_cases.description: All 7 students returned with their score remainder

hints: The % operator computes the modulo (remainder after integer division).
MOD(score, 10) is an equivalent function call.
explanation: The % operator returns the remainder of integer division. Examples: 95 % 10 = 5, 82 % 10 = 2, 77 % 10 = 7, 63 % 10 = 3, 91 % 10 = 1, 54 % 10 = 4, 88 % 10 = 8. You can also write MOD(score, 10) for the same result.
